scheme.label: Predictive torque control with no modulator (finite control set)
scheme.about: The same torque-to-current reference, with the regulator and the modulator replaced by a controller that picks the legs' states directly. Its switching frequency is not set: it follows from the weight on commutations.

sources.limit: the torque of the drive's current limit
sources.rate: the whole torque limit in half the speed loop's time constant, 1/(2·ωs)
sources.jerk: that rate reached in a quarter of the speed loop's time constant

sources.voltage_share: the share of the ideal voltage the stage gives at the design point (dead time, shortest pulse and the devices' drop), as the loss engine takes it

sources.weight: no weight on commutations: the least current error, whatever it costs in switching

tuning.rule: a twentieth of the 100,000 Hz sampling rate

assumes: each axis is taken alone: the cross-coupling between the axes is fed forward exactly, or the rotor is still
no voltage limit and no current limit is reached
the rotor's angle is known exactly, and the speed with no lag
the shaft has inertia and nothing else
missing: Predictive current control (finite control set) (predictive) has no linear transfer function: it chooses among a finite set of states, and is read from the run in time alone
